artifacts.name: letter to governor
artifacts.body:
Dear {{ recipient.salutation }},

Thank you. On behalf of the over 2000 Massachusetts residents who have written to you about ICE flights at Hanscom Field, we want to acknowledge your leadership. Your December 12, 2025 letter to DHS Secretary Noem and Acting ICE Director Lyons named what is happening plainly and courageously: "Flying these residents out of state and away from their support systems and legal counsel — often within hours of arrest — is intentionally cruel and purposely obstructs the due process and legal representation they are owed." Your subsequent letters demanding that GlobalX and Eastern Air Express stop contracting with ICE, and your signing of Executive Order No. 650 on January 29, 2026, demonstrate exactly the kind of leadership Massachusetts
needs right now.

We are writing because we believe the next step is clear — and it is within your direct authority. Executive Order No. 650 prohibits state facilities and property owned or controlled by the Executive Department
from being used by federal immigration officers "as a staging area, processing location, or operations base for civil immigration enforcement efforts." Massport is not a private entity. It is a public instrumentality of the Commonwealth, established by the Legislature under Chapter 465 of the Acts of 1956, with five of its seven
board members appointed by you. It owns and controls Hanscom Field outright as state property. Your order already covers Hanscom. Massport's continued facilitation of ICE transfer operations is noncompliance with your own Executive Order. You must make full compliance with Executive Order No. 650 a prerequisite for any
appointments to the Massport Board.

The constitutional stakes make inaction unconscionable. The Massachusetts Constitution of 1780 guarantees that the right of habeas corpus "shall be enjoyed in this Commonwealth in the most free, easy, cheap, expeditious and ample manner" (Chapter VI, Article VII). The Legislature has not suspended this right. Every detainee involuntarily flown out of Hanscom — often within hours of arrest, before their family or lawyer knows they are gone — is being denied a constitutional protection they are guaranteed under Massachusetts law. This is
not a federal question. It is a Massachusetts question, and it is happening on Massachusetts-controlled property.

Massport is also in direct violation of its own regulations. ICE charter operations at Hanscom use aircraft with 150–180 seat capacity, in direct violation of 740 CMR 25.03, which prohibits commercial air passenger service using aircraft with more than 60 seats without a waiver from the Executive Director. The FAA defines Section 121 charters — such as those operated by GlobalX and Eastern Air Express — as commercial air passenger service. The regulation expressly prohibits waivers for regular and recurring flights. The Massport Board has enforced compliance on lessees and contractors before, as with its 2014 and 2019 living wage resolutions. The authority and obligation are identical here.

We are grateful for everything you have done. We are asking you to go further. We ask that you direct your appointees on the Massport Board to enforce Executive Order No. 650 and 740 CMR 25.03 immediately, and publicly call on CEO Richard Davey to act. The outcome we seek is straightforward: all involuntary detainee flights from Hanscom Field must either be halted entirely, or a state-supervised due process screening program must be in place guaranteeing that every person boarded onto such a flight has had their habeas and due process rights fully respected under Massachusetts law before departure.

You have the authority. You have already said this must stop. We are asking you to use one to enforce the other.

Sincerely,

{{ writer.address_block }}

artifacts.name: Short Email
artifacts.subject: 3rd Request: Stop Violating the Massachusetts Constitution at Hanscom Field
artifacts.body:
Dear Chief Executive Officer Davey, Board Chair Jacobs, and Vice Chair O'Brien,

You and Governor Healey have received over 2000 letters from Massachusetts residents requesting you take seriously your responsibility to "comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and constitutional guarantees" as demanded in a unanimously approved letter from HFAC. You already are directly violating your own regulation at 740 CMR 25.03 by not limiting or granting waivers to large jet charter flights at Hanscom that have more than 60 seats, and fully meet the definition of "commercial air passenger service" as defined by the FAA. You are also facilitating a serious violation of the due process rights of Massachusetts residents as guaranteed in our state constitution.

• The 10th amendment to the US constitution protects State Sovereignty by providing to states all powers not assigned to the federal government. Traditionally this has included police powers.
• The Federal guarantee of due process says no person shall be "deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law."
• The oldest part of Common law is the right of habeas corpus.
• The Massachusetts Constitution, written in 1780 says "The privilege and benefit of the writ of habeas corpus shall be enjoyed in this Commonwealth in the most free, easy, cheap, expeditious and ample manner, and shall not be suspended by the Legislature, except upon the most urgent and pressing occasions, and for a limited time not exceeding twelve months" (Chapter VI, Article VII).
• As the legislature has not suspended this ample right, detainees involuntarily flown out of Hanscom field are being denied the due process rights they enjoy in Massachusetts.

We demand you immediately implement a screening program for all involuntary transfers boarded onto flights at Hanscom Field, and that such a screening process guarantee us, the citizens of the Commonwealth, that due process rights of each person flown involuntarily out of Hanscom have been fully respected. In addition, we demand you halt all large charter operations at Hanscom Field unless they have received a waiver from the Massport Executive Director in compliance with 740 CMR 25.00.

Sincerely,
{{ writer.address_block }}

Dear Chief Executive Officer Davey, Board Chair Jacobs, and Vice Chair O'Brien,

You have received over 2000 individual letters and emails asking you to take action to stop ICE flights from operating at Hanscom Field. I am writing again because the continuation of these flights is illegal under your own rules, under the Governor's Executive Order, and under the Massachusetts Constitution itself.

In her December 12, 2025 letter to DHS Secretary Noem and Acting ICE Director Lyons, Governor Healey wrote: "Flying these residents out of state and away from their support systems and legal counsel — often within hours of arrest — is intentionally cruel and purposely obstructs the due process and legal representation they are owed."

On January 29, 2026, Governor Healey reinforced this position by signing Executive Order No. 650, which explicitly prohibits state facilities and property owned or controlled by the Executive Department from being used by federal immigration officers "as a staging area, processing location, or operations base for civil immigration enforcement efforts." Although Massport describes itself as independent, it is a creature of state legislation — established by the Massachusetts Legislature as "a body politic and corporate and a public instrumentality of The Commonwealth of Massachusetts" under Chapter 465 of the Acts of 1956 — with five of its seven board members appointed by the Governor, and it owns and controls Hanscom Field outright as state property. Therefore Executive Order No. 650 applies to operations of Massport and its FBO tenants at Hanscom.

The constitutional stakes could not be higher. The Federal guarantee of due process says no person shall be "deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law." The Massachusetts Constitution of 1780 goes further, guaranteeing that the right of habeas corpus "shall be enjoyed in this Commonwealth in the most free, easy, cheap, expeditious and ample manner" (Chapter VI, Article VII). The Legislature has not suspended this right. Detainees involuntarily flown out of Hanscom are being denied constitutional protections they are guaranteed under Massachusetts law — often before their families or lawyers even know they are gone.

You are also in direct violation of your own regulations. ICE charter operations at Hanscom use aircraft with 150–180 seat capacity, in direct violation of 740 CMR 25.03, which prohibits commercial air passenger service using aircraft with more than 60 seats without a waiver from the Executive Director. The FAA defines Section 121 charters — such as those operated by GlobalX and Eastern Air Express — as commercial air passenger service. The regulation expressly prohibits waivers for regular and recurring flights. The Board has enforced compliance on lessees and contractors before, as with its 2014 and 2019 living wage resolutions. The authority and the obligation to act here are identical.

We demand you immediately implement a screening program for all involuntary transfers boarded onto flights at Hanscom Field that guarantees the due process and habeas rights of each person have been fully respected before departure. We demand you halt all large charter operations at Hanscom Field unless they have received a waiver from the Massport Executive Director in compliance with 740 CMR 25.00. And we demand you honor Governor Healey's Executive Order No. 650 by ending Massport's role as a staging ground for federal civil immigration enforcement.

You cannot defy Governor Healey's explicit order by not taking any action. The Massachusetts Constitution demands action. Our Governor has demanded action. Over two thousand Massachusetts residents have demanded action. Make these changes now.

Sincerely,
{{ writer.address_block }}
